correctness.rationale: Grouping j by gcd(n,j) proves H(n)=h(n)/n with multiplicative h and h_p(a)=(p^(2a+1)+1)/(p+1), so denominator has ell iff v_ell(n)>sum_{p != ell}v_ell(h_p(v_p(n))). All h_p(a) are odd, hence delta_2=1/2. When ell=3 or ell=1 mod6, Phi_6 has a nonzero root mod ell; infinitely many primes in that residue class contribute positive ell-valuation already at exponent one. Divergence of reciprocal primes in the progression and finite-prime CRT independence, bounded variance and Chebyshev force numerator valuation above any fixed threshold for density one; hence denominator ell density zero. For ell=5 mod6 Phi_6 has no root, so only p^a with a>=2 can contribute. Tail density sum_{p>Y}1/p² vanishes; finite-prime valuation independence gives the stated convergent positive Euler product, each factor 1+O(p^-2). A p=-1 mod ell and a=(ell-1)/2 gives a positive valuation by LTE and proves strict <1/ell. At ell=5 primitive residue order shows only p=-1 mod5 contribute, with v_5(h_p(a))=v_5(2a+1). Independent rational summation checks H(n)=h(n)/n for n<=350; independently counting n<=10000 with 5|den gives 1994. This is not a proof of asymptotics.
